rows.evidence: Q1: Abstract and Sections II-V report the authors' own development of a three-layer irrigation automation platform (sensor modules, Raspberry controller, servers), three scheduling/control modes and software testing; Fig. 2 shows the realized sensor module.
rows.notes: The paper is an engineering/system-architecture description within a UNDP/RoAid project. It reports no crop yield, quality or drought-condition data of any kind; no field trial, no plantation results. The claim that automated sensor-based systems maintained constant yield and quality under drought is not supported by anything in the text. The study only shows that the system was built (precondition).

rows.evidence: Q1: Abstract, Sections II-V and Figs 1-6 describe the authors' own hardware/software development and software testing of the irrigation control platform.
rows.notes: No drought-risk, yield or quality outcomes are reported. The paper describes system architecture, controllers, communication (GPRS), servers and reporting applications only. Drought is not mentioned beyond the policy introduction. The study shows only that the system exists (precondition), not that it maintained yield/quality under drought.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections II-V and Fig. 1 report the authors' own design and realization of the platform integrating wind turbine/PV power, sensor modules, valve/pump control, GPRS link, background/public servers and reporting applications (Fig. 6 example report).
rows.notes: The study describes the platform (renewable-energy integration, remote control, data reporting) but reports no measurement of water saved, irrigation efficiency or water-consumption optimization; Fig. 6 is an example report diagram, not a result. Section V only asserts generically that closed-loop control ensures optimal water consumption. Efficient irrigation management as a water-conservation outcome is not evidenced; the paper demonstrates only the enabling system.

rows.evidence: Q1: Section III and Fig. 2 report the authors' own realized integrated sensor module including soil humidity and temperature sensors at two depths.
rows.notes: The study only describes that the sensor module measures soil humidity at two levels and that closed-loop control uses these data; it reports no soil-moisture data, no irrigation scheduling outcome, no water-use-efficiency measurement, and no grapes or any crop. The claim of improved water use efficiency is not supported; the paper only establishes the monitoring capability (precondition).

rows.evidence: Q1: Section III and Fig. 2 report the authors' own sensor module with soil humidity/temperature sensors at two levels.
rows.notes: No crop, grape, yield or quality data appear anywhere in the paper. Soil moisture sensing is described as a component of the system, but no effect on grape quality or production is measured or reported. Only the precondition (sensor-based monitoring) is shown.

notes: Conference paper (Secrieru et al. 2017) describing the architecture, hardware and software of an autonomous drip/sprinkler irrigation remote control and monitoring platform in Moldova. It is a system-development/design paper with software testing; it contains no agronomic experiment, no water-use or yield measurements, no grapes, no drought trial, and no statistics. Q1 answered 'yes' because it reports the authors' own development results, but none of the claimed effects (yield/quality maintenance, water conservation, WUE, grape quality) are evidenced. Text appears complete; figures partly garbled (Fig. 1 labels in Romanian, Fig. 5/6 fragments).
